record.context_brief: Definition of divergence in information geometry
record.original_question: What should count as the right notion of a divergence function in information geometry when positivity and metric-generation by second derivatives are not always required, for example in singular statistical models?

evidence.quote: Give a good definition of the ”divergence” function in information geometry. Many divergence functions have been studied in information geometry, such as KL-divergence and Bregman divergence. The geometry of dual connections does not require the positivity of the divergence, and the geometry of singular statistical models does not require the fact that the Riemannian metric is induced from the second derivative of the divergence. What should the divergence function be in information geometry?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a foundational/conceptual one: identifying the "right" axiomatic notion of divergence that subsumes KL, Bregman, dual-connection (non-positive) and singular-model settings. No standard reference provides a single agreed-upon definition meeting all stated requirements; current literature offers various partial frameworks (contrast functions, pre-divergences, statistical manifolds admitting torsion, singular semi-Riemannian information geometry) but no universally accepted unifying definition. The problem appears open as a definitional/foundational question.

status_evidence.title: Information Geometry and Its Applications (Amari)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard treatment uses positivity and Hessian-induced metric in defining divergence; discusses Bregman and f-divergences.
status_evidence.claim: Classical definition assumes positivity and metric from second derivatives, leaving non-positive / singular cases outside the standard framework.

status_evidence.title: Singular semi-Riemannian geometry and information geometry (survey literature)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses extensions of information geometry to singular models without standard Hessian-metric structure.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work extends information geometry to singular settings but does not settle a unified definition of divergence.
